questions.question: You see the reduced visibility warning sign ahead. What is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Maintain your speed; visibility will improve naturally.
Slow down, increase your following distance, and switch on dipped headlights if necessary.
Accelerate to pass the area quickly before visibility worsens.
Switch off your headlights and continue at normal speed.

questions.question: What should you do when you see the congestion ahead warning sign?

options.text: Maintain your speed, because traffic will clear quickly.
Slow down, keep a safe following distance, and be prepared to stop if necessary.
Accelerate to pass through the area before the traffic builds up.
Switch lanes frequently to find a faster route through the congestion.

questions.question: You see the horses and riders ahead warning sign. What is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Maintain your speed, because horses will always stay on the side of the road.
Slow down, be prepared to stop, and give plenty of space when passing horses.
Accelerate to pass the horses quickly so you don’t delay traffic.
Sound your hooter repeatedly to warn the horses to move faster.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you of?

options.text: Rhinos on the road ahead.
Elephants on the road ahead.
Hippos on the road ahead.
Antelopes on the road ahead.

questions.question: You see the hippo ahead warning sign near a river or wetland. What is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Maintain your speed; hippos usually stay in the water.
Slow down, stay alert, and be prepared to stop if a hippo is on or near the road.
Accelerate to pass quickly before a hippo appears.
Sound your hooter to warn the hippo to move away.

questions.question: You see the electrical shock warning sign. What should your first action be?

options.text: Ignore the sign; it only applies to maintenance workers.
Keep an eye out for electrical cables on the road ahead.
Touch the electrical cable quickly to see if it is really electrified.
Lean over the electrical cable to get a better view of the cable.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you of?

options.text: Strong gusts of wind.
Faster moving vehicles kicking up dust.
Clear wind ahead.
A wind farm ahead.

questions.question: You are driving on a rural road and you see the narrow bridge warning sign ahead. What is the MOST correct action to take?

options.text: Maintain your speed, because other vehicles must give way when you reach the bridge first.
Slow down, keep to your side of the road, and be prepared to stop if another vehicle is approaching.
Overtake slower vehicles before entering the bridge to avoid being delayed.
Sound your hooter continuously while approaching the bridge to warn oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You are approaching a structure with the one vehicle width structure warning sign. Another vehicle is already entering the structure from the opposite side. What should you do?

options.text: Accelerate quickly so you can squeeze through before the other vehicle reaches you.
Stop and allow the other vehicle to pass through first before you enter.
Drive halfway in and wait inside the structure for the other vehicle to pass.
Sound your hooter to claim right of way and continue through.

questions.question: You are driving on a two lane road and you see the road narrows from both sides warning sign. What is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Maintain your lane but move closer to the centre of the road to avoid hitting the sides.
Slow down, keep well within your lane, and be alert for oncoming traffic or obstacles.
Accelerate to pass the narrow section quickly before other vehicles approach.
Change lanes immediately to the opposite lane to avoid the narrowing.

questions.question: You are driving on a two lane road and see the road narrows from the right side warning sign ahead. What is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Move slightly to the left within your lane, slow down, and be cautious of the narrowing right side.
Move to the right to let the road widen naturally on the left side.
Maintain your speed and lane, because the road will naturally adjust for your vehicle.
Accelerate to pass the narrow section before other vehicles arrive.

questions.question: You are driving on a two lane road and see the road narrows from the left side warning sign ahead. What is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Move slightly to the right within your lane, slow down, and be alert for the narrowing left side.
Move to the left to use the space that is narrowing.
Maintain your speed and lane, because the road will adjust automatically.
Accelerate to pass the narrow section quickly before any oncoming vehicles arrive.

questions.question: You are driving and see the uneven roadway warning sign ahead. Which of the following is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Maintain your speed; the uneven surface will not affect your vehicle.
Slow down and hold the steering wheel firmly to maintain control over bumps and keep an eye out for potholes.
Swerve slightly to avoid the uneven parts of the road.
Accelerate quickly to pass the uneven section before it causes any damage.

questions.question: What should you immediately do when you see this sign?

options.text: Maintain your current speed; your car can handle the bumps.
Slow down before reaching the speed bumps and drive over them carefully.
Accelerate to pass over the speed bumps quickly so you don’t lose momentum.
Sound your hooter to warn pedestrians and continue at normal speed.

questions.question: You see the slippery road warning sign ahead. What is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Maintain your speed, but turn the steering wheel sharply to avoid skidding.
Slow down, avoid sudden braking or sharp turns, and drive carefully.
Accelerate slightly to pass the slippery area quickly.
Sound your hooter to warn other drivers and continue at normal speed.

questions.question: You see the falling rocks warning sign on a mountain pass. What is the MOST correct action to take?

options.text: Slow down, be alert for rocks on the road, and avoid stopping unnecessarily near the area.
Accelerate quickly to pass through the area before rocks can fall
Drive as close as possible to the cliff face to avoid rocks falling into the road.
Stop immediately under the cliff and wait until the danger has passed.

questions.question: You see the general warning sign on a road. What is the MOST correct action to take?

options.text: Ignore it; it is only a suggestion and not a real hazard.
Slow down and drive with caution, being prepared for any type of hazard ahead.
Accelerate to pass the area quickly before the hazard appears.
Sound your hooter and continue at normal speed, because the danger is probably minor.

questions.question: You see the emergency flashing light warning sign ahead. What is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Maintain your speed, because the flashing light is only for decoration.
Slow down, be prepared to stop, and keep an eye out for any hazards ahead.
Accelerate to pass the area quickly to avoid slowing down traffic.
Sound your hooter continuously to warn the emergency vehicles you are coming.

questions.question: You see the jetty edge ahead warning sign. What is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Maintain your speed; the sign is only for boats, not vehicles.
Slow down, stay well within your lane, and be alert for the edge of the road or riverbank.
Accelerate quickly to pass the area before other vehicles or pedestrians appear.
Stop immediately and reverse, because the road is too dangerous to continue.

questions.question: You see the crosswinds warning sign ahead. What is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Maintain your speed and lane; crosswinds only affect large trucks.
Slow down, hold the steering wheel firmly, and be prepared for sudden gusts.
Steer slightly into the wind at all times to counteract it.
Accelerate to pass the area quickly before the gusts hit.

questions.question: You see the drift warning sign ahead. What is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Maintain your speed; your car can handle slippery surfaces.
Slow down, avoid sudden steering, braking, or accelerating, and drive carefully.
Accelerate slightly to pass the slippery section quickly.
Steer sharply to counteract any slipping you feel.

questions.question: You see the low flying aircraft warning sign ahead. What is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Maintain your speed and ignore any sudden noise or shadows from aircraft.
Slow down slightly, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, and stay alert for sudden distractions.
Accelerate to get past the area quickly before any aircraft pass overhead.
Stop in the middle of the road to watch the aircraft.

questions.question: You see the agricultural vehicles warning sign ahead. What is the MOST correct action?

options.text: Maintain your speed, because tractors always stay to the side of the road.
Slow down, be prepared to stop, and give way if necessary to slow-moving agricultural vehicles.
Accelerate to pass any slow moving vehicles before they block the road.
Sound your hooter repeatedly to warn the tractor to speed up.
